Here's a regex for an ISO 8601 calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`):

```
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}` matches the four-digit year.
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` matches the month, 01–12.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` matches the day, 01–31.

It matches `2026-10-01`.

It checks the format and the ranges, but not whether the day exists in that month. `2026-02-31` would still match. Calendar validity (leap years, 30-day months) is best handled by parsing the date in code.

To find dates inside longer text, drop the anchors and use word boundaries instead:

```
\b\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])\b
```
